messages:
maya: Heads up — we're seeing p95/p99 regressions since 03:40 UTC for a handful of customers (large conversational workloads). Suspect: KV/prefix cache thrash after yesterday's routing & compaction tweak. p95 ~600ms (baseline ~180ms), p99 ~1.8s. Attaching traces and a short dump below.

aj: Support ticket created: #CS-1289. I've pulled metrics: prefix_cache.miss_rate jumped from 8% -> 63% on shard-7 between 03:35-03:42. Eviction rate spiked and warmup hitrate is near zero.

kevin: Repro locally with replayed traffic (same customer prompt set) — I can repro p95 jump when we enable prefix-key-hash-normalization + LFU eviction on small cache sizes. Steps: 
1) set LFU, cache_size=256MB, enable normalization flag 
2) replay customer A traffic at 2x QPS
Result: miss rate and eviction churn go crazy.

julia: Logs snippet from prod (filtered):
```
[03:38:12] prefix_cache: miss key=customerA:conv:turn:hash=0x9ac3 count=1
[03:38:12] eviction: evicted key=customerB:conv:turn:hash=0x1f3a age=12s
[03:38:13] kv_warmup: prefill_attempt=0
```
Seems like hot keys are not sticking and old keys keep getting evicted quickly.

david: FYI we rolled LFU -> default-two-days-ago as part of memory-optimization PR #2246 (to avoid hot-key starvation), but it looks like with normalized keys the cardinality exploded. LFU ends up evicting items that are actually hot because normalization made different prefixes look similar? possible bug in normalization namespace.

maya: Immediate mitigation options — pick one: 
- A) Temporarily bump prefix-cache pool size for affected clusters (+40%) and enable warmup prefill for the next 10m.
- B) Rollback normalization flag for serving tier (fast toggle).
- C) Switch eviction policy back to LRU for this pool.
Which is fastest?

aj: B is fastest (flip flag). I can push a config flip to 10% -> 0% traffic in 2m. C is also easy but requires config rollout per shard (slightly longer). A needs infra approval for memory spike.

kevin: I'll prepare a short rollback patch and smoke tests. Also adding a temporary hotkey whitelist for top 50 observed prefixes to avoid churn.

oncall-bot: Incoming change request logged: CR-3819. Deployment window 03:58-04:05 UTC.

support-bot: Notified customers: CS-1289, CS-1292, CS-1297 — we sent a holding message and ETA 30m.

maya: Proceed with B + hotkey whitelist. Kevin, coordinate with aj on the patch. Julia, monitor metrics. David, open a follow-up ticket to investigate normalization bug and eviction interaction.

kevin: Patch rolled at 03:59 (rolled normalization_flag=false for serving pool A -> 0%):```
curl -XPOST https://ops-api/flags/normalize_prefix -d '{"pool":"serving-A","enabled":false}'
```
Smoke tests: sample traces show prefix_cache.miss_rate dropping from 63% -> 12% within 90s.

aj: Post-mitigation numbers at 04:02 UTC: p95 220ms, p99 430ms for affected customers. Eviction churn down ~80%. Hotkey whitelist prevented further immediate spikes.

julia: Verified traces: KV hit ratio rose from 37% -> 78% after flip. No increase in OOM or memory alerts.

david: Created follow-up EPIC: INF-789 "prefix-key-normalization-collision" and linked to forensic logs + repro. Include: key hashing audit, unit tests for normalization idempotency, and eviction policy interactions.

maya: Postmortem/next steps: 
- Short term: leave normalization_flag=false until we ship fix behind a safer hashing scheme.
- Medium term: add metric alert for prefix_cache.eviction_rate > 10% sustained for 2m and auto-scale option to increase pool by 25% for 5m.
- Long term: stronger hotkey detection + sticky routing for heavy conversational customers, and migration plan for normalization change.

support-bot: Customer follow-up messages queued; asking for a brief RCA to send by EOD.

maya: I'll draft the RCA. Quick runbook notes to add to oncall guide: 
- If p95 spike reported and prefix miss_rate > 40%: check recent flag flips / PRs affecting eviction or normalization.
- Temp mitigations: flip normalization flag, switch to LRU, or increase pool capacity.
- When flipping flags, whitelist top prefixes to avoid immediate cold-start.

kevin: Agree. Also adding a lightweight stress test to CI that replays high-prefix-cardinality traffic and asserts miss_rate < 20% under baseline cache size.

aj: Closing CS-1289 as mitigated, will keep monitoring until EOD.

maya: Thanks team. We'll regroup tomorrow for a longer postmortem and timeline for INF-789 fix. :thumbsup:
